source: Temporal Technologies, 'The State of Development Report 2026', dated August 25, 2026. No named individual author on the page. Opened in full via the Markdown version https://temporal.io/reports/state-of-development-2026.md (canonical page https://temporal.io/reports/state-of-development-2026). The linked PDF (downloads.ctfassets.net/.../The_State_of_Development_2026_-_Temporal.pdf) was not opened.
data_type: Survey (commissioned online panel via Qualtrics, self-report), with some free-text word-frequency charts.
sample_and_method: 'Between April 29 to May 25, 2026 we commissioned the survey provider Qualtrics to solicit responses from 650 respondents currently using AI agents following strict criteria around role and location. We removed all responses we considered low quality and were left with 554 respondents.' Location: two-thirds US, one-third UK/EMEA. Roles: 'Engineer / AI engineer (25.6%), VP / director of IT (13.9%), data engineer (11.9%), DevOps/platform engineer, architect, data scientist, CEO / management'. Experience: 32.9% 6-10 years, 48.4% 11+ years. Company size: 251-1000 employees 29.2%, 51-250 22.7%, 1,001-5000 18.8%. Industry: software 37.5%. All respondents already use AI agents. The page's meta description says 550 and the intro says '500+'; the methodology and chart totals say 554. 'Successful' cohort is self-reported.
vendor_interest: Yes. Temporal sells a durable-execution/orchestration platform marketed for AI agents; the report ends with 'Develop AI agents 50% faster with an orchestrator...' and compares Temporal users with others.
headline_figures: 'No surprise, though, some of this exuberance is driven by leadership: CEOs, management, VPs, and directors were 1.4x more likely to say their organization is ‘very successful’ (43.7% vs 32.4%).'
Pull quote: 'Leadership is 35.1% more likely to say their organization is ‘very successful’ compared to the engineers.'
Summary: '84.5% believe they are better than their competitors at using AI agents. This is somewhat driven by executives, who are 35.1% more likely than their teams to say this.'

Chart 2.5, 'In your opinion, how successful is your company at using AI agents relative to peers?': Very successful 201 (36.3%), Somewhat successful 267 (48.2%), About the same 63 (11.4%), Somewhat less 11 (2%), Much less 8 (1.4%); total 554.
'A great majority of teams we polled think they’re in the 85th percentile of agent excellence which is, statistically, unlikely. (Possible, but unlikely.)'
'91.1% say agents have ‘improved’ or ‘revolutionized’ their productivity' (Chart 2.1: Improved 72%, Revolutionized 19.1%, No impact 6.7%, Worsened 1.8%).
'A 70.8% leap in AI agent use: 80.8% use agents daily, up from 47.3% a year ago'
'Trust is high. One quarter (24.7%) completely trust the outputs. A majority (60.8%) at least somewhat trust. Only 4.0% distrust.'
'41.1% encounter issues daily or more; 9.0% say “continuously”'
'79.8% say token and compute cost is a limiting factor'
'44.6% are less stressed than one year ago (the successful are much less stressed)'
metric_layer: Perception only: self-rated organisational success relative to peers, self-rated personal productivity, adoption frequency (input/usage), prototype-to-production time (self-reported delivery speed), trust, issue frequency, cost as a factor, stress. No measured delivery, quality or financial outcome data.
respondent_role_split: Yes for the key item: 'CEOs, management, VPs, and directors' 43.7% vs (engineers) 32.4% say their organisation is 'very successful' at using AI agents relative to peers. The report describes this as '1.4x more likely' and, in the pull quote, '35.1% more likely ... compared to the engineers'. Subgroup sizes are not given in the text. Most other splits are 'successful' vs 'everyone else' or Temporal users vs non-users, not by role.
workload_signal: Mixed. Stress vs one year ago: 14.1% much less, 30.5% slightly less, 22.7% same, 26.7% slightly more, 5.8% much more stressed. 'Respondents worry that no matter how much more efficient they grow, leadership will just keep raising expectations. People at successful companies are less likely to say this.' (no figure given). 'The more stressed the team, the more issues they encounter: 52.2% of those who are more stressed encounter agent issues daily, versus 32.4% of those who are less stressed.' Free-text on stress weighted 'reduces' highest, with 'workload' and 'increases' also present. No hours or time-correcting-AI figures; 'there is a difference between trusting enough to proceed and trusting enough to put your name on the commit.'
definition_of_value_offered: No. 'Successful' is self-rated relative to peers ('When we discuss those who are “successful at using AI agents,” that is self-reported data'). Productivity is self-rated ('improved'/'revolutionized'). The report does not define what paying off should mean or how to measure it; it frames success around solving state, debugging, cost and reliability (its product's area).
removal_counterfactual: None. All respondents currently use AI agents; no data on teams without them.
key_quotes: "No surprise, though, some of this exuberance is driven by leadership: CEOs, management, VPs, and directors were 1.4x more likely to say their organization is ‘very successful’ (43.7% vs 32.4%)."
"A great majority of teams we polled think they’re in the 85th percentile of agent excellence which is, statistically, unlikely."
caveats: Vendor-commissioned panel survey of existing agent users only, so selection favours enthusiasts; self-report throughout, including the 'successful' cohort. Internal inconsistency on the headline ratio: 43.7/32.4 = 1.35, which the report calls both '1.4x more likely' and '35.1% more likely'; 1.35 rounds to 1.3x or 1.35x, not 1.4x. Safer to quote the raw percentages. The comparison group is labelled 'the engineers' in the pull quote but its exact membership (all non-leadership roles, or engineer titles only) is not defined; the summary calls it 'their teams'. Subgroup n not given, so no significance test is possible. Sample size stated variously as 550, 500+ and 554 (554 is the methodology figure). Note 32.4% also appears as an unrelated stress statistic in the same report; do not confuse them. The question asks about the company's success relative to peers, not whether AI paid off financially.
access: Primary opened in full (the report's official Markdown rendering on temporal.io, including methodology and chart tables). Not opened: the PDF version, so any PDF-only content or differences were not verified; leadership/engineer subgroup sizes not published in the page.
